summary: Backend-only validation of the KIWI 'already-invoiced items reappear as pending' fixes. Created /app/backend/tests/test_invoice_double_submit_guard.py (18 tests) and /app/backend/tests/test_invoice_concurrent_race.py (1 TOCTOU probe). VERIFIED: (a) POST /api/invoices returns 409 with detail 'N compra(s) ya están facturadas: <item> (factura <id>). Refresca la página y vuelve a intentarlo.' when any purchase_id already has invoice_id — no new invoice doc is written and the purchases keep pointing at the original invoice (integrity stays healthy); mixed pending+invoiced also 409 and the pending one stays pending; (b) all-pending happy path still creates the invoice and links purchases; (c) regressions intact: unknown purchase_ids -> 400 'Algunas compras no fueron encontradas', empty purchase_ids -> 400, PUT /invoices/{id}/add-items still 400 'ya está en otra factura' for cross-invoice purchases (and still succeeds for pending ones), annul frees invoice_id so annulled purchases can be re-invoiced (new guard does not over-block); (d) GET /api/admin/clients/{customer_id}/purchase-integrity returns the documented shape, is_healthy=true + empty arrays for a healthy client and for a non-existent client (counts 0), normalizes lowercase customer_id, 403 for client role, no Mongo _id leaked, and correctly flags all three corruption classes injected directly in Mongo (orphan with reason='not_in_invoice_purchase_ids', purchase_ids_not_found, cross_invoice_conflicts). Seed client C5557 reports healthy (4 invoices / 20 purchases). Also re-ran the FULL existing suite: 319 passed / 17 failed — the same 17 pre-existing failures listed in iteration_18 (EMERGENT_LLM_KEY missing, employees/audit RBAC hole, clients-debts KeyError, stale legacy expectations); none are caused by this iteration's changes. TWO NEW DEFECTS FOUND (see backend_issues).

critical.issue: The new guard is read-then-write (TOCTOU) and does NOT close the real production race. Reproduced with 5 truly parallel identical POST /api/invoices (tests/test_invoice_concurrent_race.py): status codes were [200, 409, 409, 200, 409] -> TWO invoices created for the SAME purchase_ids, and GET purchase-integrity immediately reported is_healthy=false with cross_invoice_conflicts=2 — i.e. the exact KIWI corruption is still reproducible on a fast double-click / two simultaneous tabs. Fix: make the claim atomic instead of pre-checking, e.g. purchases.update_many({'id': {'$in': ids}, 'tenant_id': tid, '$or': [{'invoice_id': None}, {'invoice_id': {'$exists': False}}]}, {'$set': {...}}) and require modified_count == len(ids), otherwise roll back the inserted invoice and raise 409 (or add a unique index / findOneAndUpdate per purchase before inserting the invoice).

minor.issue: No is_deleted guard: a soft-deleted purchase (is_deleted=true) is happily included in a new invoice (returns 200). PUT /invoices/{id}/add-items already rejects these ('está eliminada'). Add the same check + exclude is_deleted in the purchases query.
Missing Authorization header returns 422 (FastAPI validation) instead of 401 — app-wide behaviour, cosmetic only.

orphans_in_invoice spreads the whole purchase doc (**p) into the response, so it can grow large for corrupted clients; cross_invoice_conflicts detection is O(purchases x invoices) with two .to_list(20000) loads — acceptable for a debug endpoint but should be capped/projected if exposed in the UI. Also no auto-repair action is offered, so ops still needs manual Mongo work.

action_items: CRITICAL: make the purchase claim atomic in POST /api/invoices (conditional update_many on invoice_id null + modified_count check, rollback of the inserted invoice on mismatch). The current pre-check still allows two concurrent submits to create two invoices over the same purchases (reproduced, cross_invoice_conflicts=2).
Add the is_deleted guard to POST /api/invoices (parity with add-items) and exclude soft-deleted purchases from the purchases query.
Consider a repair endpoint/script that uses the purchase-integrity output to re-link or clean the KIWI-style corruption already present in production data.
Pre-existing from iteration 18 (still open): employees/audit-logs RBAC hole + password_plain leak, EMERGENT_LLM_KEY missing (all uploads/OCR dead), clients-debts KeyError 'available'.
critical_code_review_comments: create_invoice: guard at ~5959 and update_many at ~6066 are not in the same atomic operation and there is no transaction; the invoice document is inserted BEFORE the purchases are claimed, so a losing concurrent request leaves a duplicate invoice behind. Claim purchases first (conditionally) and only insert the invoice if the claim succeeded.
create_invoice purchases query lacks {'is_deleted': {'$ne': True}} — deleted items can be billed.
purchase-integrity returns full purchase documents inside orphans_in_invoice; project only the needed fields to keep the payload bounded.
server.py is ~9300 lines — should be split into routers (invoices, wallet, admin, shipments) per the 700-line guideline.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_invoice_double_submit_guard.py tests/test_invoice_concurrent_race.py -q -s -p no:randomly`. Two tests are EXPECTED to fail until the main agent fixes them: (1) test_invoice_concurrent_race.py::test_parallel_identical_submits_produce_single_invoice — proves the guard is not atomic (2 invoices for the same purchases, cross_invoice_conflicts=2); (2) TestGuardInteractions::test_soft_deleted_purchase_can_still_be_invoiced — create_invoice accepts is_deleted purchases. Everything else about the 409 guard and /purchase-integrity works exactly as specified. The 17 other suite failures are pre-existing (see iteration_18.json). Frontend still untested since iteration 16.
rca_of_the_issue: Original KIWI bug: POST /api/invoices unconditionally ran purchases.update_many($set invoice_id=new) for the submitted ids, so a stale/duplicate submit reassigned already-invoiced purchases, leaving the old invoice with orphan purchase_ids; the recalculation chain then resurfaced those items as pending. The new 409 pre-check fixes the common sequential case (verified) but because the check and the update_many are separate non-atomic steps and the invoice is inserted before the purchases are claimed, two simultaneous requests still both pass the check — reproduced with 5 parallel submits producing 2 invoices and cross_invoice_conflicts=2. Mitigation: conditional/atomic claim of the purchases (invoice_id null in the update filter) with modified_count verification and rollback.
